> Source workbook: `tk-syllabus-comparison-doc-v6.xlsx` (EASA TK Syllabus Comparison Document, version 6, ECQB 2026).

## How to use this scaffold

- Use the subject headings and syllabus references as the filing structure for your notes.
- Add concise aide-memoire material under each learning objective.
- Keep the `Exam` and `TK` module tags visible so the guide remains aligned with the BIR scope.
- Use `CBIR` and `IR` tags to see where BIR knowledge also supports the later CBIR/full IR path.

### Tag legend

- `Exam M1/M2/M3`: BIR exam module indicated in the source workbook.
- `TK M1/M2/M3`: BIR theoretical knowledge/basic knowledge module indicated in the source workbook.
- `CBIR`: learning objective is also tagged for CBIR(A).
- `IR`: learning objective is also tagged for the full IR.

    - **`062.06.01.00` Global navigation satellite systems (GNSSs)**
      - **`062.06.01.01` General**
        - `062.06.01.01.01` State that there are four main GNSSs. These are: USA NAVigation System with Timing And Ranging Global Positioning System (NAVSTAR GPS); Russian GLObal NAvigation Satellite System (GLONASS); European Galileo (under construction); Chinese BeiDou (under construction). [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.01.02` State that all four systems (will) consist of a constellation of satellites which can be used by a suitably equipped receiver to determine position. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
      - **`062.06.01.02` Operation**
        - `062.06.01.02.01` State that there are currently two modes of operation: standard positioning service (SPS) for civilian users, and precise positioning service (PPS) for authorised users. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.02` SPS was originally designed to provide civilian users with a less accurate positioning capability than PPS. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.03` Name the three GNSS segments as follows: space segment; control segment; user segment. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.09` State that an ionospheric model is used to calculate the time delay of the signal travelling through the ionosphere. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.11` State that satellites are equipped with atomic clocks which allow the system to keep very accurate time reference. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.12` State that the control segment comprises: a master control station; a ground antenna; monitoring stations. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.14` State that GNSS supplies three-dimensional position fixes and speed data, plus a precise time reference. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.15` State that a GNSS receiver is able to determine the distance to a satellite by determining the difference between the time of transmission by the satellite and the time of reception. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.16` State that the initial distance calculated to the satellites is called pseudo-range because the difference between the GNSS receiver and the satellite time references initially creates an erroneous range. [TK M2; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.17` State that each range defines a sphere with its centre at the satellite. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.18` State that there are four unknown parameters (x, y, z and Delta t) (receiver clock error) which require the measurement of ranges to four different satellites in order to get the position. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.19` State that the GNSS receiver is able to synchronise to the correct time reference when receiving four satellites. [TK M2; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.06.01.02.20` State that the receiver is able to calculate aircraft ground speed using the space vehicle (SV) Doppler frequency shift or the change in receiver position over time. [TK M2; IR]

[Exam M2; CBIR; IR]

        - `062.07.01.01.04` Define accuracy as the conformance of the true position and the required position. [TK M2/M3; IR]

        - `062.07.01.01.06` Define integrity as a measure of the trust that can be placed in the correctness of the information supplied by the total system. Integrity includes the ability of a system to provide timely and valid alerts to the user. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]
        - `062.07.01.01.07` State that, unlike conventional navigation, PBN is not sensor-specific. [Exam M2; TK M3; CBIR; IR]

        - `062.07.05.05.11` State that the FAS data block is a standard data format to describe the final approach path. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]

        - `062.07.05.06.01` State that RNP AR APCH requires authorisation. [Exam M2; CBIR; IR]
